cases.customer_question: How should qualification planning handle HID11 cases where some required PTS tests may not be executable because the profile support in PTS is still incomplete or beta quality?
question_variants: What if HID11 PTS cases cannot run?
Can manual interoperability testing replace unavailable PTS coverage?
When are HID11 unsupported PTS cases identified?
How do beta-quality HID11 tests affect qualification?
What happens if PTS cannot execute required HID11 cases?
cases.actual_issue: Managing qualification risk when HID11 qualification depends on PTS coverage that may not fully support all ICS-linked test items.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The customer worried that some HID11 qualification tests might not be executable in PTS because the HID11 test support was still incomplete. The consultant explained that older HID11 qualifications had cases that PTS could not execute and that some HID11 TCRL entries were still marked as member-defined quality. The recommended process was to first compare the HID11 ICS against available PTS coverage and then perform manual peer-device testing if unsupported mandatory cases remained.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that earlier HID11 registrations encountered cases such as HID11/HOS/CDD/[ID] that could not be executed in PTS. The consultant stated that HID11 test support remained partially beta quality in the TCRL and therefore some ICS-dependent mandatory items might still lack complete automated PTS coverage. The consultant advised first reviewing the HID11 ICS against the generated PTS test item list to determine whether all required cases are available. If unsupported required cases remain, the applicant or software development partner must execute device-to-device alternative testing and create substitute interoperability evidence.
cases.decision_logic: Qualification obligations are determined by the required test coverage associated with the ICS selections. If mandatory cases are not executable in PTS, alternative evidence must be generated to satisfy qualification requirements.
cases.final_recommendation: Finalize the HID11 ICS early, compare it against the generated PTS test coverage, and prepare for supplemental device-to-device interoperability testing if mandatory HID11 cases are unavailable in PTS.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Failing to identify unsupported mandatory HID11 test items early can create unexpected manual testing work, schedule delays, failed submissions, or incomplete qualification evidence late in the project.
